# Event path origins and separate native views

Updated: 2026-10-19 12:52 CEST. Start: `8282cca55`.
Source main: `184bba662`. Merge: `a3cf692cb`. Proof: `776875701`.

## System guarantee

Fresh construction always finishes in the Lean model. Under the stated
guard conditions, its result represents exactly the specified finite trees.
A completed supported root reduction with empty inherited constraints
preserves that language. General outer completion and Haskell refinement
remain open. Read `notes-current-system-claim.md`.

## Full row origins along a path

`SourceCurrentProjectionPathOrigins.PathOrigin` uses one physical view.
Its root case retains an epsilon Origin of the complete selected row.
Its child case retains an epsilon-origin parent row, an exact natural
child index and the remaining PathOrigin. It preserves full guards and
ordered children. Mu and union exposure belong to the epsilon origin;
they do not add a child index to the path.

`project_read` starts from actual Project and Read graphs and their
selected Spine. Initial semantics, costs and availability remain explicit.
The later reader needs semantic support, costs and forward Keeps from
projection return. The caller supplies a view that grows from the actual
read return. No whole-value closedness, guard heap or desired origin law
is a premise.

The Spine induction derives internal support through actual ordered
projection and read prefixes. Actual suffixes connect every internal read
to the final read return. Actual completed Head reads supply their full
row Origin at the common view. This does not transport an arbitrary
Origin through growth. It uses the completed read and its replay theorem.

`occurs` prepends a literal ordinary event occurrence to an observed
continuation. It retains the residual natural child path. It does not
follow stored Mu bodies, union members or observational unfolding rows.

## Actual class-fold composition

`SourceCurrentRecursiveEventPathOrigins.fold` consumes the previous
actual event-observation theorem. The original false gate, actual Required
preparation and actual FoldReads retain their existing support premises.
The result is an ordinary Route in the FINAL fold value, or an actual
earlier event contains the exact first recursive value.

The recursive alternative now retains a PathOrigin of the same full row
from that event. Its path is the event's literal residual followed by the
recursive value's actual remaining observation path. Its view is the
completed selected read heap. Actual projection and read effects derive
Keeps from the recursive projection entry to that heap. The captured
event Source remains at its earlier supported entry.

Preparation and fold share the returned forest, with separate supported
heaps. This result does not construct a complete chronological outer call.
PathOrigin is row ancestry. It does not construct a Project of the
unchanged whole event or assert that a deep row is an event root row.

## Native calls with a separate physical view

`SourceCurrentNativeOriginViewBranches.returned` retains a captured checked
reader with its actual native history and returned cell. Its selected row
Origin uses a separate valid physical view. Actual forwarding normalizes
the request to one chosen writer. No native memo state is assigned to the
physical view. The view need not grow from the query heap in this generic
contract; its Origin and validity are explicit.

`request` derives codecs, history, physical facts and the chosen returned
writer from an actual completed request. The Origin still uses the
separate view. The conditional Mu result keeps that writer's actual body
execution at the captured reader and an actual stored unfolding at the
physical view. It does not identify these two executions.

`ordinary` first derives that the actual ordinary compiler returned an
ordinary value. Its epsilon Origin therefore selects a literal physical
row. The theorem recovers both indexed input rows, the full conjunction,
the exact paired child request and Good child endpoints. Both original
operand children have strictly smaller mass than their respective query
inputs. No source-row positivity premise is needed. The generated output
child need not have smaller mass.

The ordinary conclusion retains child-heap growth into the captured query
reader. It does not export native Retained from that child return or its
returned-cell writer. Repeated normalization of the child still needs
that memo provenance. A later proof must recover it from the actual
ordered row and child schedules. No child-entry History is assumed.
The existing row producer retains the actual edge-call return in the
captured reader. Its warm edge-writer receipt then keeps only heap growth.
The next foundation must retain the native memo relation from that same
earlier edge-body return to the chosen checked reader, as the existing
node-writer receipt does.

`union` recovers the exact original member index, actual ordered prefix,
child call and suffix. The selected member has smaller source mass. Its
child return is retained in the captured reader and has Forwarded there.
The same complete row has Origin at the physical view of that child result.
No mass bound is placed on the generated child result.

`reference` retains the actual entered name, captured read, operand order
and resolved child call. Forwarded belongs to the captured checked reader.
The full row Origin remains at the physical view. Reference resolution
has no strict mass claim.

A PathOrigin child supplies its exact parent epsilon Origin, selected
child and remaining path to these native handoffs. A nonplain deep row
does not prove that the earlier parent or Head row is nonplain.

## Constructed checks

The path check builds an event wrapper around the existing two-row source.
An actual projection selects outer row index 1 and internal Mu-read index
0. The actual calls derive PathOrigin from the source at [0]. A literal
event occurrence at [0] gives the combined event path [0,0]. The selected
deep row has no root Origin from the event. The theorem proves both facts.
It assumes no whole-event Project.

The native-view check builds a closed native query and derives its actual
Trace, Good states and history. A new physical edge increases the heap's
edge count. An actual row Read then supplies Origin at this distinct
later heap. The native request handoff keeps its writer at the captured
query return. The result is ordinary; the check does not exercise its
conditional Mu unfolding conclusion. It assumes no native history at
the physical view.

Neither check instantiates the full original-false-gate outer composition.
Neither asserts finite productivity, a language failure or a Haskell defect.

# Upstream ordered enumeration and optimization coverage

Updated: 2026-10-19 12:42 CEST. Main: `184bba662`.
Merge: `a3cf692cb`. Previous verified checkpoint: `8282cca55`.

The merge adds changes from PRs #68, #87 and #88. Twelve paths change.
Six existing Haskell files take the exact upstream bytes. OrderedFrontier
is one new Haskell file. The other 261 existing Haskell files retain their
bytes. The merge retains both the local constructor-probe repair note and
all new upstream changelog entries. No local Haskell behavior patch is added.

## Ordered cursor

`cfta/src/Data/CFTA/Enumeration.hs` adds an optional ordered cursor. It
uses shallow child expansion and a separate frontier scheduler. Existing
eager entry points still call the original enumeration path.

The order contract requires admissible partial bounds and monotone pure
deterministic observers. An invalid bound can be reported after earlier
outputs. The contract leaves constrained cyclic truncation equivalence
open. Work and capacity limits count scheduler jobs and queue entries.
They do not bound callback cost or resident memory. Strengthening replaces
shared state; it does not validate the caller's monotonicity obligation.

`SourceCurrentEnumerationOrder` describes earlier edge ordering.
`EnumerationCPSRuns` describes the earlier enumerateFully composition.
Neither models the new frontier or caller-defined global keys. Their
checked laws do not establish the new cursor's implementation correctness.

## Template exclusion

`cfta/src/Data/CFTA/Template.hs` prepares a catalogue of finite template
subtrees and uses catalogue identities during exclusion. It combines
positive child patterns and rejects a requirement to both match and fail
the same pattern. The implementation uses sequences for ground groups.

The stated contract requires finite total templates, lawful equality and
ordering, and catalogue/group sizes that fit Int. Catalogue preparation
can force template parts that earlier execution did not inspect. The
preservation claim concerns the complete finite-term language. Run
multiplicity and recursive cutoff streams remain separate properties.

`SourceTemplateShapeSplits.splits_exact` models the earlier root-shape
filter. Its scope excludes the full forced/dying/ground schedule and
interned exclusion. It supplies no proof of the new prepared catalogue,
positive-pattern conjunction or identity-conflict pruning.

## Recursive subsumption

`cfta/src/Data/CFTA/Interned/Operations.hs` shares mandatory child pairs
through a visited worklist. Each narrow edge must have one compatible
unconstrained wide edge. Ambiguity discards the worklist and restarts the
original search from the original roots with fresh assumptions.

The review found no cross-alternative assumption leak. This inspection is
not an equivalence proof. `MergedAlternativesSubsumption.check` models the
earlier ancestor-stack search. The shared worklist needs an additional
equivalence or soundness proof. Existing termination requires a finite
pair inventory; it does not cover arbitrary physical unfolding.

## Typing notation

`cfta-generator/src/Data/CFTA/Gen/Typing/Do.hs` adds
`draw generator = [drawn generator]` and re-exports drawn. This is additive
syntax for the existing drawn premise. The new test compares it with an
explicit rule. No test run is claimed. Generator/refinement frontend
correspondence remains a separate whole-library obligation.

## Review and preservation

All twelve changed paths were inspected. No demonstrated new correctness
defect was found. No Haskell build or test was run. Existing upstream test
assertions are source evidence, not passed execution evidence.

Further validation should cover capacity pause/resume, strengthening of
queued completed work, invalid bounds and constrained recursive order.
Template conjunction and duplicate-ground cases need finite exhaustive
comparison. Shared-cycle subsumption needs comparison with ambiguity
fallback. These are follow-up validation tasks, not new repair requests.

The refresh manifest pins every changed post-merge path. All earlier Lean
sources retain their bytes. Existing counterexamples, repairs, marked
drafts, stashes and other worktrees remain preserved. Root FINDINGS records
this coverage change before the older repair entries. Publication awaits
direct approval. No push or board write is attempted.

# Current system claim

Checked against the live theorem statements on 2026-10-19.
Read `notes-current-recursive-event-source-read.md` for the latest checkpoint.

In simple technical English: fresh construction always finishes in the
Lean model. Under the stated guard conditions, its result represents
exactly the finite trees specified by its expression. A completed supported
modeled root reduction with empty inherited constraints preserves that
exact language.
The root theorem derives the logical startup cache and guard facts.
Field allocation, validity, guard coverage and numeric resources remain
explicit. General termination and Haskell correspondence remain open.

## Constructed root guarantee

`SourceCurrentConstructedRootCall.root_call` starts from a literal closed
FreshOrdinary build from the empty source heap. An actual original-field
allocation history must cover all expression guards. Its starting equality
interner must be valid. The modeled caller and its global memo tables
start logically empty. The inherited value is the actual empty allocation.

If the bounded root call returns, and Fits, carrier and scheduled Room
hold, its returned value is available and, for every ambient interpretation,

`L(result) = evaluate(original expression)`.

The statement covers the full source syntax, including nested raw and
smart binders and retained earlier cache writers. It supplies no semantic
Context, guard heap, Frame, root availability or desired result law.
`AllocatedPartialInitialization.constructed` derives the logical Context.
`ConstrainedCapGuardExecution.closed_heap` derives the initial guard heap.
`ConstructedOuterInitial.node_call` derives the actual NodeLaw.
`InternedGuardedExecution.closed_language` identifies the input language
with its independent least finite-tree syntax semantics.

This endpoint takes actual construction and root-call completion as
premises. The separate `InternedFreshOrdinaryClosedCompletion.closed_complete`
theorem supplies a completed fresh build from empty captures and caches for
each source expression in the model. General outer reduction completion
remains open. These results do not prove concrete Haskell cache startup,
host integer adequacy or whole-library termination.

A completed class fold now retains descendant structural RowAt sources in
the same initial forest slot, or actual native/Head events in earlier class
phases. Indexed ordinary event lifts retain separate canonical output and
raw row indices and exact child slices. Each phase derives its physical
support and writer history from its actual completed tail. A literal
bounded-worker return derives this graph from initial Frame, Fits and
numeric reservations. Its support and memo premises remain explicit.
The earlier root-only FoldFlow cannot consume arbitrary descendant RowAt.
Actual projection and complete row reads now retain indexed recursive
read histories, including Mu unfolding. A completed node edit derives an
ordinary source at the same path in the original input, with the same
symbol, full guard and arity, or an actual native/Head cut with its exact
remaining projection and selected read. The producer constructs path
safety from the original false gate and Required Origin. Actual edit
effects derive projection support at the returned heap. Reader semantic
support, forward Keeps and the reader guard heap remain explicit.
